newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid fuel prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid fuel prices steady to lower.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to down slightly Thursday in lackluster trade, with stable crude, firmer bunkers and forecasts for colder East Coast weather buoying the complex despite soft utility demand.
"Right now, there aren't a lot of people who need oil, but it's all tied to weather," said one cash trader, noting hopes for better utility demand next week when colder weather hits.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was little changed on the day at $19.25-50 a barrel, with November one percent paper talked in the mid-$19s and December unchanged at about $20, traders said.
Poor utility demand and good avails pressured NYH 0.3 percent high pour down slightly to about $21, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH were unchanged, with 2.2 percent still quoted in the $18.50-75 range.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent notionally fell a quarter to $17.75-$18.00, while three percent held steady at $16.25-50.
Traders said 120,000 barrels of USG eight gravity one percent sold late Wednesday at $17.30.
USG November three percent paper was done at $17.05.
New York City gate swing gas was unchanged Thursday in the mid-$2.90s/mmBtu compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.08/mmBtu equivalent.
